create.name: Buddhist Geeks
create.bio:
Buddhist Geeks is a long-running dharma channel and publication presented by Vince Fakhoury Horn under the motto "Evolving Dharma". Its YouTube channel opened in March 2012 and now holds more than 350 videos, and the same work appears as a newsletter and podcast on buddhistgeeks.org. The recent material is mostly practical meditation teaching from a pragmatic, experimental angle: the stages of jhāna and access concentration, kasina practice with fire and breath, metta and compassion, equanimity, and how to give a dharma talk.

Alongside these short teachings, the channel keeps a run of longer conversations in which Western teachers look back on the people who trained them, such as Sharon Salzberg remembering Dipa Ma, Trudy Goodman on Kōbun Chino Otogawa and Leigh Brasington on Ayya Khema. Earlier interviews feature teachers including Judith Blackstone on embodied nondual realisation. Formats range from guided sessions and five-minute explainers to hour-long dialogues, and it suits meditators who like to ask how classical Buddhist practice works in a modern, networked life.

Political content on the channel and site: left out the uploads "Dharma & Empire", "Trump as Imperial Policy Returned", "How Empire Occupies the Psyche", "Is the Insight Tradition Complicit in Genocide?", "TPOT, Palestine, & True Bodhisattvahood", "The Cost of Silence" and "Working Class Dharma"; the site's sitemap also lists posts such as "The Palestine Test", "Mindful Zionism", "Real Progressive Dharma" and "Dharma and Empire". buddhistgeeks.org is a Substack publication; only pages on the custom domain were read (home, /about, /podcast, /sitemap.xml). No substack.com page or link was opened.
Presenter named only as the copyright holder "Vince Fakhoury Horn" on buddhistgeeks.org; he is not on Spiritpedia (dev names file checked for Horn).
Our teachers interviewed on the channel: judith-blackstone, sharon-salzberg, trudy-goodman (Sharon Salzberg and Trudy Goodman videos included); Ramona Lisa Ortiz-Smith's video is also included.
Photo is the channel's logo avatar (cartoon head with glasses), not a person.
No offerings or free resources: the site's about page says full archive access needs a subscription, and no item with its own clearly free URL could be confirmed without JavaScript; videos only (12).
